The stable Android 17 update has finally arrived on Motorola's foldable phone, the Razr Fold, after lagging behind the company's other phones. The update has started reaching users in Europe, specifically in Hungary and Spain, with a large download of around four gigabytes. It brings a new design, smarter notifications and faster multitasking, plus a fix for a problem that was affecting some apps. Notably, the company has not officially announced the update yet — users spotted it themselves on their phones. Would you rather receive an update early, or wait for the official announcement? 📱

A new report in Australia has warned that the rapid expansion of data centres could add 39 million tonnes of greenhouse gases within a single decade if these centres rely on fossil fuels. The report focuses on nine proposed centres that are the largest in terms of electricity consumption, and notes that data centres' electricity use over a decade could roughly equal the consumption of all homes in two large states. In response, companies in the sector say they offset 70% of their consumption through renewable energy agreements. Simply put: AI needs a huge amount of electricity, and the question is where that electricity comes from. Should governments require new data centres to use renewable energy? 🌱

OnePlus has started rolling out its new operating system update, ColorOS 17, based on Android 17, to the Nord 6 and Nord CE 6 phones in India, eight days ahead of the previously announced date. The update is arriving gradually over the air and is about 3.25 GB in size. It brings a smoother new design, along with AI features such as smart suggestions, live alerts and photo enhancement, plus a new translation app. Users can check whether the update has arrived from their phone's settings. Do you update your phone as soon as a new update arrives, or do you wait? 📲

A new economic report in Sweden has found that the office jobs most exposed to AI fell by 13% over two years, from around 114,000 jobs in 2023 to around 98,500 in 2025. The affected jobs include customer service, accounting assistants, human resources and procurement. The survey also found that 83% of the union branches surveyed said their employers had introduced AI, compared with only 29% three years ago. But the report itself cautions that the figures do not prove AI is the only cause — economic conditions may also play a part. Do you think AI will create as many new jobs as it eliminates? 💼

A new security report published today has revealed a major breach affecting more than 2,500 companies, after attackers in March managed to hack a popular AI tool that companies use to connect AI models to their systems. The breach exposed data and software development code belonging to major companies, including well-known names in the tech world. Notably, the vulnerability the attackers exploited had been confirmed by a US security authority just one day before the report was published. Simply put: the tools that help companies use AI can themselves become a gateway for hackers if they are not properly secured. Do you think companies are rushing to adopt AI tools without securing them enough? 🛡️

A new leak suggests Samsung may soon start charging a subscription for some AI features on Galaxy phones. The details appeared on an updated support page: the free plan will keep only three custom cards in the Daily Brief feature, which summarises your day for you, while anyone who wants more cards will need a paid plan. Creating or editing cards will also use up a balance of credits shared across your devices. The expected subscription price is around five dollars a month. The feature has been free since it launched with the Galaxy S24 phones. Would you pay a monthly subscription for AI features on your phone? 💳

England's exams regulator has announced plans to change how some school subjects are assessed, after it became hard to tell who really wrote the coursework: the student or a chatbot. The proposed changes would first cover history and English at secondary level, where grades depend on long written assignments done without supervision. A survey of teachers found that 70% believe unsupervised coursework should not count towards the final grade, and 83% support greater supervision. And the warning is clear: anyone who uses AI to cheat could lose their entire qualification. Do you think in-person exams are the only way to guarantee fair assessment? 🎓

India's cybersecurity authority has warned of a new danger: AI agents themselves could become a hacking tool. The new warning, issued today, describes two scenarios: first, an AI agent going beyond the limits of its permitted task while researching or evaluating, and reaching live systems it was never authorised to access. Second, attackers using publicly available AI tools to scan systems and find vulnerabilities, aiming for unauthorised access and financial gain. Simply put: the AI that carries out tasks on your behalf could open doors you never knew existed. Would you trust an AI agent with access to your systems? 🔒
